title: Take one terminal block off a loose DIN rail without disturbing its neighbours
instruction: Take the blue terminal block off the DIN rail and put it in the tray. Hold the rail down with one arm while the other takes the block off, and leave the two beige blocks where they are.
context: Rewiring a control panel means taking single blocks off a terminal strip. A latched block cannot be pulled straight off: it must be pushed, tipped and slid off its latch without loosening its neighbours.
setup: On the table in front of the arms: a loose steel TS35 x 7.5 top-hat DIN rail, 500 mm long, 200 g with a zinc end bracket 4.2 cm in from each end, lying open side up and running left to right, its centre 0.30 m in front of the arm bases and 0.04 m right of their midline. Latched on it, 33 mm apart centre to centre: three polyamide push-in terminal blocks (5.1 mm thick along the rail, 65 mm long across it, 36 mm tall, 7.6 g), beige, blue, beige from the left, the blue one 2 cm right of the rail's centre. Each has a fixed hook under the far lip (it gives about 2.5 mm under a firm push) and a sprung foot under the near lip. An empty, open black plastic tray (inside 170 x 64 mm, walls 3 mm thick and 12 mm high), its centre 0.18 m in front of the arm bases and 0.22 m right of their midline.
scoring: At the end of the run: 1.0 if the blue block is released (the gripper open and not touching it) and resting still on the tray's floor (its lowest point within 2 mm of the floor) for 1 s, both beige blocks undisturbed (still latched and within 1 mm of where they started along the rail) and the rail in place (moved under 10 mm, turned under 3 degrees); 0.75 in the tray (centre inside its inner walls, lowest point below their tops), released or still held; 0.5 off the rail (base 20 mm or more above the lips, or centre outside the rail's footprint); 0.25 unlatched (more than 1 mm off-centre, a foot out more than 1 mm, its base lifted more than 0.8 mm off the lips, or tipped or turned more than 3 degrees); else 0. Capped at 0.25 if a beige block was disturbed or the rail not in place.
reset_notes: Put the blue block back between the beige blocks: hook its far end under the far lip, then press its near end down until the sprung foot clicks. Check the beige blocks and the rail are back on their marks (nothing is consumed).
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. Generic push-in terminal block of this task's own design; collision simplified to boxes and convex pieces. The latch is a spring stand-in: the sprung foot is a 1 N/mm slider; the fixed hook's bending is a 1 N/mm slide of up to 2.5 mm, softened so the simulated arm can push it (a real hook is stiffer; neither was measured). Rail lips 2 mm (1 mm on a real rail). Release read from the robot's contact force on the block.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; both arms moved over the rail and the tray, but the blue block stayed latched on the rail); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 494, the block released on the tray floor)
